findings.title: Loose typing in new script and test code under the strict-pyright rule
findings.description: `_status(...)` is annotated `-> object` but is passed to `check_dataset_edge`, which takes `subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]`. The same file has bare `-> dict` return annotations on `_request`, `_unit` and `_coverage`, and bare `list` for `exhausted`. In `scripts/cutover_304_first_purchase.py` (`judge`), `origins = {}` has no annotation. The rules include tests in strict pyright and treat zero errors as a merge blocker. I did not run pyright, so these are likely violations, not confirmed ones. Annotate them as `CompletedProcess[str]`, `dict[str, Any]`, `list[ExhaustedRequest]` and `dict[RequestKey, datetime]`.

findings.title: Resubmit origin matching ignores product
findings.description: `resubmit_origins` keys on `(schema, start, end)` only, and takes the earliest `requested_at` when ES and GC share a range. The docstring says this on purpose. The result errs toward refusing: a resubmit is rejected if either product's original predates the cutover start, which may reject a legitimate one. The cost is a false stop, not an unwanted purchase.

findings.title: Ceiling derivation and `--estimate` flow are sound
findings.description: Ceilings are derived from the estimate and rounded up to a multiple of `CEILING_STEP_USD`. The full run still requires the ceilings to be set. `--estimate` skips only the ceiling checks, writes no state and buys nothing. Tests cover each of these paths, including the 89, 90 and 6.3+4 rounding cases.

findings.title: `purchase_verdicts` and `purchase_accounting` fail explicitly
findings.description: Every parse failure raises `CutoverError` with its own message, with no silent defaults. Each `except` re-raises with `from exc`, so the handlers meet the exception-handling rule. `purchase_verdicts.py` is about 294 lines, which is within the ~300-line guideline.
